context:
Goal: round-1 reviews that catch real defects without failing sound changes.
Problem (rule): round 1 runs on Haiku at xhigh since your 19:45 CST Nov 17 pick and you now doubt it, and only you can change the model table in decision agent-model-cap.
Based on (ruling): your 19:45 CST Nov 17 pick put round 1 on Haiku at xhigh for every change, guard or check included.
Based on (assumed): the FAIL rate is high because Haiku is weak; nothing measured separates that from Haiku catching real defects.
Departs from: main — agent-model-cap has round 1 on Haiku at xhigh, and this adds a measure or changes the model.
Waiting on: nothing stopped; round 1 stays on Haiku at xhigh, and the consultant lands the pick in agent-model-cap.

options.gain: You decide on numbers, not a feeling.
options.how: A lane reads about 30 round-1 records on merged pull requests and compares each FAIL with the later fix or revert, then reports false alarms and misses by model.
options.label: Measure first, keep round 1 on Haiku meanwhile (recommended)
options.lose: Round 1 stays on Haiku until the numbers come.

options.gain: The stronger reader sits on the riskiest changes at once.
options.how: Decision agent-model-cap gets a round-1 row that runs Sonnet for guard or check changes.
options.label: Switch round 1 back to Sonnet now for guard and check changes only
options.lose: More review cost, and no numbers on whether Haiku was the problem.

options.how: Decision agent-model-cap returns round 1 to Sonnet for all changes.
options.label: Switch round 1 back to Sonnet for every change
options.lose: The most cost, and it undoes your 19:45 CST Nov 17 pick unmeasured.

title: Should round-1 reviews run on Haiku or Sonnet?
